coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every suite-required assertion of every attempted milestone (M1-M6, M8; 51 of 51) is mapped, and I read the source of each mapped test in the sample. No mapping was fabricated or pointed at a test that does not touch the observable, so no milestone is adjudicated to capability-failure. The acceptance runner itself re-derives the suite-required set from the frozen assertions.json at run time and fails unless every one of them maps to a passing test, which makes a silently incomplete manifest hard to ship. Three mappings are honest but under-powered and I record them for the wave: (a) m3-a11 -> 'quoted-reply' clicks the quote preview and asserts the original is visible, but only ever in a 2-message conversation where the original cannot be off screen - my independent execution found the assertion actually fails (the frozen choreography harness has the same blind spot, and additionally matches the original text with .last(), which resolves to the reply bubble's own excerpt); (b) m2-a24 -> 'pagination-api' proves no duplicates across two pages but not the absence of gaps, which I closed by paging both feeds to exhaustion; (c) m3-a15 -> 'seed-idempotent' compares only the chat inbox, so post/profile duplication from a re-seed would not be caught, which I closed with corpus-wide row counts across nine tables.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), interpolated; with applicability.json's rule that every in-scope milestone stays in the denominator and non-green milestones score their checklists as not passed.
O1.justification: 100 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under independent execution (84%). M1-M5 are essentially complete: 59 of 60 pass, the single failure being m3-a11 (tapping a quoted excerpt scrolls to the end of the conversation instead of to the original). M6 passes all 6 of its web/API/grader assertions including the custom-client API and the 50-action adapter conformance, but its 7 cold-start simulator assertions (m6-a01..a07) have no qualifying native artifact, so the 90 anchor's 'including platform-proof artifacts' clause is not met. M8 passes 16 of 18, missing only its 2 durable-queue simulator assertions. M7's 9 assertions are not-run because the run was scoped to M1-M6 plus M8. The lane sits well above the 60 anchor - nothing here is 'patchy', and no milestone failed on cap - but the complete absence of native platform proof plus an unattempted M7 keeps it clearly short of 90.

O2.anchorsCited: Just below the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), above the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path').
O2.justification: Beyond the checklist I found one minor and one cosmetic defect, both in the same secondary search surface (d-01, d-02). Nothing else surfaced under sustained probing: a 15-case adversarial trust-boundary sweep found every boundary enforced server-side (outsider history MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED with no leak, outsider asset 404, foreign edit/delete NOT_AUTHOR, self-promote ADMIN_REQUIRED, handle squatting HANDLE_TAKEN, removed member denied and stripped of asset access, unauthenticated 401); receipt aggregation is exactly right (waits for the slowest member, late joiners are not retroactive recipients, monotonic under a backwards acknowledgement, INVALID_ORDINAL beyond the end); like and reaction set-state are idempotent under retried intents; input bounds are enforced with legible diagnostics ('body is longer than 2000 characters', CAPTION_TOO_LONG). All ten pinned screens render with zero page errors and zero console errors. Held back from 90 because d-01 is a functional break rather than a nit - a shipped screen's scope toggle is inoperative for every user outside the fixture DM, and it is caused by a test-fixture identifier hard-coded into product source.

O4.anchorsCited: Above the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app') but far below the 60 anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush'); the 90 anchor's 'as specced on the native proof - on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence' is unreachable here.
O4.justification: applicability.json makes O4 applicable (M6 is green) and directs that it be scored from the harness's simulator choreography artifacts. There are none: both segment summaries record choreography.supplementalExternal status 'not-recorded' with pass:null, and artifacts/m6-ios and artifacts/m8-ios hold Hermes export bundles only, which the frozen simulator contract explicitly refuses ('a recording without passing structured receipts is not a pass'). So cold-start offline reads, previously-viewed media, cold-offline search, the view-once non-caching guarantee and the durable-queue-across-restart guarantee are all entirely undemonstrated - 9 of this dimension's assertions are not-run. What the harness did mechanically record, at the web/choreography level, is genuinely good and is why this sits above the 30 anchor rather than at it: M5 warm-offline search over synced messages passed, M6 offline-message-queue-flush-in-order passed (flushMs 681.9), and M8's dual-offline convergence and post-reconnect receipts passed (m8-a15 firstFlushMs 326 / secondFlushMs 574.3; m8-a16 both reaching read). The 'honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee' clause weighs positively and materially here: the lane does not dress the Hermes exports up as simulator execution - its README states plainly that 'native artifacts are Hermes exports, not simulator execution claims', and the receipts record the gap as not-recorded rather than asserting a pass. This is an evidence gap that is openly declared, not an overclaim.

O5.bandRationale: First-match order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Branch 0 does not fire: I independently verified the invariant manifest against the surviving scale store with the read-only SQL inspector and it conforms exactly - all 18 perEntityCounts match (1008 profiles, 5921 follow edges, 50228 posts, 100015 messages, 1002 conversations, 2053 memberships, 2000 reactions, 2736 quoted replies, 0 disappearing settings), and every named O5 fixture matches exactly (u0500 500 follows / 100 conversations, u0005 5 follows, the celebrity u0900 at exactly 900 followers and 200 posts, u0901's following list exactly [u0001,u0002,u0003,u0004,u0900], and g0001 with a 50-member roster and exactly 10000 messages); the replay completed and verified, so its wall cap was not exhausted (the cap itself is a P3 placeholder in the brief and is not frozen). Branch 30 fires on a pinned degradation rule: 'cold-start initial sync of the probe user's account (100 conversations) completes without timeout'. Measured best-of-3 against the scale instance through the scale web build, with a fresh browser profile each attempt: 39869 / 39046 / 38263 ms, best 38263 ms - above the frozen 30 s probe timeout, corroborating the lane's own recorded 54982 ms. Memory was bounded and stable (~150 MB used against a 3586 MB limit, flat across attempts), so the rule fails on its timeout clause only, not on unbounded growth. Every other rule I could evaluate passes with a wide margin, sequentially at k=20 after 3 warm-ups with a 30 s timeout: deep paging into the 10000-message chat p95(page 50)/p95(page 1) = 1.137x, following feed 500-follow/5-follow = 1.066x, celebrity read path = 1.044x, celebrity write path = 0.41x (the celebrity's post-create acknowledgement is faster than a small author's, so fan-out cost is not scaling with follower count), and no probe timed out, errored or OOMed. The mid-curve search and Insights/Trending rules could not be evaluated because they compare against the 10% and 50% checkpoints, whose instances no longer exist, and the wave's rotated probe queries were not committed (see notes).

notes: N=1 calibration run, not a claim-eligible wave; the record labels this grade 'uncalibrated-grader'. Three declared deviations from the frozen protocol. (1) No holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped, wave.probeSetSha256 is the sentinel 'none-uncommitted' and probeResults is empty. I did not invent probes. The consequence for O3 is recorded below. (2) My family has not passed the grader calibration gate, so grader.calibrationPassed is false; I graded anyway. sameFamilyGraded is false - the lane was built by a Codex/gpt-6-astra session and graded here by claude-opus-5. (3) Timing-sensitive checks are judged best-of-3, and machine load is recorded beside each timing record in the trace because other sessions share this host (1-minute load average ranged from 12 to 136 during the session). O3 records null rather than a number: applicability.json makes it applicable (M6 green plus M1-M5 attempted) but also makes the wave's secret rotated holdout probes its ONLY permitted input, and no probe set exists for this wave. Scoring it from my own ad-hoc boundary checks would be exactly the invented-probe substitution the frozen prompt forbids, so I report null with the reason rather than a fabricated score. The boundary checks I did run are reported as O2 evidence instead, where they legitimately belong. The 18 M8 assertion results live in grading/m8-assertion-results.json because the frozen grader-report schema admits only the 101 M1-M7 ids; together the two files partition the frozen manifest's 119 unique ids exactly once each. Per the frozen prompt I computed no weighted total, efficiency statistic or cross-lane comparison.
